title: Understand merging
summary: A merge joins histories. If two branches change the same lines differently, Git may need a person to choose the result.
introduction: A merge joins histories. If two branches change the same lines differently, Git may need a person to choose the result. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A merge joins histories. If two branches change the same lines differently, Git may need a person to choose the result.

blocks.code:
git log --oneline --all --graph
# Read the graph before deciding what to merge.
blocks.title: Understand merging

blocks.text: The graph helps you see branch history. Merging is a decision about changes, not a way to hide conflicts.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Draw two branches that edit different lines and explain why their merge may be simple.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Review and commit or safely save your work before changing branches or merging.
For more detail later, use this [Git further reading](https://git-scm.com/docs/gittutorial).

seo.title: Git: Understand merging
seo.description: Learn about understand merging in Git. Follow a small example, understand the result, and practise with a clear question.
